title: Optics
topics: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors
The eye and defects of vision

items.q: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 15 cm. Calculate its focal length in cm.
items.s: For a spherical mirror the focal length is half the radius of curvature = 15 / 2 = 7.5 cm.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: A plane mirror is turned through 10 degrees. Calculate the angle through which the reflected ray turns, in degrees.
items.s: Turning the mirror by an angle turns the reflected ray by twice that angle, so the answer is 20 degrees.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Light travels at 2.4 x 10^8 m/s in a certain medium. Taking the speed of light in a vacuum as 3.0 x 10^8 m/s, calculate the refractive index of the medium.
items.s: Refractive index = speed in a vacuum / speed in the medium = 3.0 / 2.4 = 1.25.

items.q: A lens has a focal length of -40 cm. Calculate its power in dioptre.
items.s: Power in dioptre is one hundred divided by the focal length in centimetres = 100 / -40 = -2.5.

items.q: A compound microscope has an objective of magnification 4 and an eyepiece of magnification 20. Calculate the total magnification.
items.s: The magnifications of the two lens systems multiply, so the total is 4 x 20 = 80.

items.q: Two coherent waves of wavelength 600 nm meet at a point with a path difference of 2 wavelengths. Calculate the path difference in nm.
items.s: A path difference of 2 wavelengths is 2 x 600 = 1200 nm, and since it is a whole number of wavelengths the point is bright.

items.q: A diffraction grating is ruled with 300 lines per millimetre. Calculate the distance between neighbouring lines in nm.
items.s: One millimetre contains 300 lines, so the spacing is 10^6 nm divided by 300 = 3333 nm.

items.q: Unpolarised light of intensity 500 units passes through a single polarising sheet. Calculate the intensity of the transmitted beam in the same units.
items.s: A single sheet passes half the intensity of unpolarised light, so the transmitted value is 500 / 2 = 250 units.

items.q: A laser of output power 5 mW is switched on for 10 s. Calculate the total energy it delivers in mJ.
items.s: Energy delivered = power x time = 5 x 10^-3 x 10 = 50 mJ.

items.q: A surface is lit to 20 lux by a lamp. Calculate the illuminance in lux when the surface is moved to 4 times its original distance from the lamp.
items.s: The illuminance varies inversely as the square of the distance, so it becomes 20 / (4 x 4) = 1.25 lux.

items.q: Light of wavelength 400 nm falls on a surface. Taking the product of the Planck constant and the speed of light as 1.99 x 10^-25 J m, calculate the energy of one photon in units of 10^-19 J.
items.s: Photon energy = product of the Planck constant and the speed of light divided by wavelength = 1.99 x 10^-25 / (400 x 10^-9) = 3.97 units of 10^-19 J.

items.q: An object stands 45 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Calculate the distance of the image from the mirror in cm.
items.s: Using the mirror relation, 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/10 - 1/45, so v = 12.86 cm.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: An object is placed 50 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 25 cm. Calculate the linear magnification produced.
items.s: The image distance works out to 50 cm, so the magnification is v/u = 1.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: A transparent medium has a refractive index of 2.4. Taking the speed of light in a vacuum as 3.0 x 10^8 m/s, calculate the speed of light in the medium in units of 10^8 m/s.
items.s: The speed in the medium is the speed in a vacuum divided by the index = 3.0 / 2.4 = 1.25 units of 10^8 m/s.

items.q: A ray strikes the surface of a medium of refractive index 1.6 at an angle of incidence of 40 degrees. Calculate the angle of refraction in degrees.
items.s: By the refraction relation sin r = sin 40 / 1.6 = 0.4017, so the angle of refraction is 23.69 degrees.

items.q: Light travels from a medium of refractive index 1.6 towards air. Calculate the critical angle in degrees.
items.s: The critical angle satisfies sin c = 1/1.6, so c = 38.68 degrees.

items.q: A coin lies at the bottom of a pool of water of depth 3 m. Taking the refractive index of water as 1.5, calculate the apparent depth of the coin in m.
items.s: Apparent depth = real depth / refractive index = 3 / 1.5 = 2 m.

items.q: A ray passes normally through a glass slab of thickness 8 cm and refractive index 1.6. Calculate the lateral displacement of the ray in cm.
items.s: The sideways shift is thickness times (1 - 1/refractive index) = 8 x (1 - 1/1.6) = 3 cm.

items.q: An object is placed 36 cm from a converging lens of focal length 12 cm. Calculate the image distance in cm.
items.s: From the lens relation 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/12 - 1/36, the image distance is 18 cm.

items.q: An object 50 cm from a converging lens of focal length 12 cm forms an image. Calculate the magnification.
items.s: The image distance is 15.79 cm, so the magnification is v/u = 0.3158.

items.q: Two thin lenses of power 4 dioptre and -2 dioptre are placed in contact. Calculate the power of the combination in dioptre.
items.s: Powers of lenses in contact add directly, so the combination has power 4 + -2 = 2 dioptre.

items.q: A magnifying glass of focal length 25 cm is used with the eye relaxed. Taking the least distance of distinct vision as 25 cm, calculate its angular magnification.
items.s: The magnification is one plus the least distance of distinct vision divided by the focal length = 1 + 25/25 = 2.

items.q: A ray passes through a prism of angle 45 degrees with angles of refraction 25 degrees and 20 degrees at the two faces. Calculate the angle of deviation in degrees.
items.s: The deviation is the sum of the two angles of refraction less the prism angle = 25 + 20 - 45 = 0 degrees.

items.q: A prism of angle 50 degrees produces a minimum deviation of 36 degrees. Calculate the refractive index of its material.
items.s: At minimum deviation the index is sin((A + D)/2) / sin(A/2) = sin 43 / sin 25 = 1.61.

items.q: A glass has refractive indices 1.52 for violet and 1.51 for red light. Taking the index for the middle of the spectrum as 1.52, calculate its dispersive power.
items.s: Dispersive power = (index for violet - index for red) / (middle index - 1) = (1.52 - 1.51)/(1.52 - 1) = 0.0192.

items.q: In a two slit experiment the slits are 0.25 mm apart and the screen is 2 m away. Taking the wavelength as 450 nm, calculate the fringe separation in mm.
items.s: Fringe separation = wavelength x screen distance / slit separation = 450 x 10^-9 x 2 / (0.25 x 10^-3) = 3.6 mm.

items.q: Light falls normally on a soap film of refractive index 1.33 and thickness 500 nm. Calculate the optical path difference for light reflected from its two surfaces, in nm.
items.s: The extra distance is twice the thickness multiplied by the index = 2 x 1.33 x 500 = 1330 nm.

items.q: Two coherent beams of amplitudes in the ratio 2 to 1 interfere. Calculate the ratio of the maximum intensity to the minimum intensity.
items.s: The intensity ratio is the square of the sum of the amplitudes over the square of their difference = (2 + 1)^2 / (2 - 1)^2 = 9.

items.q: Light of wavelength 550 nm passes through a single slit of width 0.5 mm. Calculate the angle at which the first minimum appears, in degrees.
items.s: The first minimum satisfies sin(theta) = wavelength / slit width = 550 x 10^-9 / 0.5 x 10^-3, giving 0.063 degrees.

items.q: A telescope objective has an aperture of 4 cm. Taking the wavelength as 650 nm, calculate the smallest angular separation it can resolve, in units of 10^-6 radian.
items.s: The limit is 1.22 times the wavelength divided by the aperture = 1.22 x 650 x 10^-9 / 0.04 = 0.1983 units of 10^-6 radian.

items.q: Light reflected from the surface of a medium of refractive index 1.6 is completely plane polarised. Calculate the angle of incidence in degrees.
items.s: The polarising angle satisfies tan(p) = 1.6, so the angle of incidence is 57.99 degrees.

items.q: Plane polarised light of intensity 600 units falls on an analyser set at 30 degrees to the plane of vibration. Calculate the intensity transmitted, in the same units.
items.s: By the cosine squared rule the transmitted intensity is 600 x cos squared 30 degrees = 450 units.

items.q: A solution has a specific rotation of 50 degrees per dm per unit concentration and is placed in a tube of length 0.25 dm at a concentration of 25 g per cm cubed. Calculate the angle through which the plane of polarisation is turned, in degrees.
items.s: The angle turned is specific rotation x concentration x length = 50 x 0.25 x 25 = 312.5 degrees.

items.q: An optical fibre has a core of refractive index 1.6 and a cladding of refractive index 1.4. Calculate the acceptance angle in air, in degrees.
items.s: The sine of the acceptance angle is the square root of the difference of the squares of the indices = sqrt(2.56 - 1.96), giving 50.77 degrees.

items.q: Light is guided along the core of refractive index 1.5 of an optical fibre surrounded by cladding of refractive index 1.46. Calculate the critical angle at the boundary, in degrees.
items.s: The critical angle satisfies sin(c) = 1.46/1.5 = 0.9733, so it equals 76.74 degrees.

items.q: An optical fibre has a core of refractive index 1.6 and a cladding of refractive index 1.46. Calculate its numerical aperture.
items.s: The numerical aperture is the square root of the difference of the squares of the two indices = sqrt(2.56 - 2.13) = 0.6545.

items.q: A short sighted person can see clearly only up to 0.5 m. Calculate the power of the correcting lens needed, in dioptre.
items.s: The lens must form an image at the far point, so its focal length is minus 0.5 m and its power is -1/0.5 = -2 dioptre.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: A long sighted person has a near point of 0.5 m and wishes to read at 0.25 m. Calculate the power of the lens needed, in dioptre.
items.s: The lens must take an object at 0.25 m to an image at 0.5 m, so its power is 1/0.25 - 1/0.5 = 2 dioptre.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: An eye can focus clearly from a near point of 0.3 m out to a far point of 2 m. Calculate the range of power of its lens, in dioptre.
items.s: The change of power is 1/0.3 - 1/2 = 2.83 dioptre.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: A point source of luminous intensity 20 candela shines on a surface placed 1.5 m directly below it. Calculate the illuminance on the surface in lux.
items.s: Illuminance = intensity / distance squared = 20 / (1.5 x 1.5) = 8.89 lux.

items.q: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 48 cm. Calculate its focal length in cm.
items.s: For a spherical mirror the focal length is half the radius of curvature = 48 / 2 = 24 cm.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Light travels at 1.8 x 10^8 m/s in a certain medium. Taking the speed of light in a vacuum as 3.0 x 10^8 m/s, calculate the refractive index of the medium.
items.s: Refractive index = speed in a vacuum / speed in the medium = 3.0 / 1.8 = 1.67.

items.q: A lens has a focal length of -10 cm. Calculate its power in dioptre.
items.s: Power in dioptre is one hundred divided by the focal length in centimetres = 100 / -10 = -10.

items.q: A compound microscope has an objective of magnification 8 and an eyepiece of magnification 10. Calculate the total magnification.
items.s: The magnifications of the two lens systems multiply, so the total is 8 x 10 = 80.

items.q: Two coherent waves of wavelength 640 nm meet at a point with a path difference of 4 wavelengths. Calculate the path difference in nm.
items.s: A path difference of 4 wavelengths is 4 x 640 = 2560 nm, and since it is a whole number of wavelengths the point is bright.

items.q: A diffraction grating is ruled with 250 lines per millimetre. Calculate the distance between neighbouring lines in nm.
items.s: One millimetre contains 250 lines, so the spacing is 10^6 nm divided by 250 = 4000 nm.

items.q: Unpolarised light of intensity 300 units passes through a single polarising sheet. Calculate the intensity of the transmitted beam in the same units.
items.s: A single sheet passes half the intensity of unpolarised light, so the transmitted value is 300 / 2 = 150 units.

items.q: A laser of output power 1 mW is switched on for 2 s. Calculate the total energy it delivers in mJ.
items.s: Energy delivered = power x time = 1 x 10^-3 x 2 = 2 mJ.

items.q: A surface is lit to 200 lux by a lamp. Calculate the illuminance in lux when the surface is moved to 4 times its original distance from the lamp.
items.s: The illuminance varies inversely as the square of the distance, so it becomes 200 / (4 x 4) = 12.5 lux.

items.q: An object stands 30 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 24 cm. Calculate the distance of the image from the mirror in cm.
items.s: Using the mirror relation, 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/24 - 1/30, so v = 120 cm.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: An object is placed 20 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 30 cm. Calculate the linear magnification produced.
items.s: The image distance works out to -60 cm, so the magnification is v/u = -3.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: A transparent medium has a refractive index of 2. Taking the speed of light in a vacuum as 3.0 x 10^8 m/s, calculate the speed of light in the medium in units of 10^8 m/s.
items.s: The speed in the medium is the speed in a vacuum divided by the index = 3.0 / 2 = 1.5 units of 10^8 m/s.

items.q: A ray strikes the surface of a medium of refractive index 1.33 at an angle of incidence of 35 degrees. Calculate the angle of refraction in degrees.
items.s: By the refraction relation sin r = sin 35 / 1.33 = 0.4313, so the angle of refraction is 25.55 degrees.

items.q: Light travels from a medium of refractive index 2.42 towards air. Calculate the critical angle in degrees.
items.s: The critical angle satisfies sin c = 1/2.42, so c = 24.41 degrees.

items.q: A coin lies at the bottom of a pool of water of depth 3 m. Taking the refractive index of water as 1.6, calculate the apparent depth of the coin in m.
items.s: Apparent depth = real depth / refractive index = 3 / 1.6 = 1.88 m.

items.q: A ray passes normally through a glass slab of thickness 4 cm and refractive index 1.4. Calculate the lateral displacement of the ray in cm.
items.s: The sideways shift is thickness times (1 - 1/refractive index) = 4 x (1 - 1/1.4) = 1.14 cm.

items.q: An object 30 cm from a converging lens of focal length 20 cm forms an image. Calculate the magnification.
items.s: The image distance is 60 cm, so the magnification is v/u = 2.

items.q: Two thin lenses of power 2 dioptre and 2 dioptre are placed in contact. Calculate the power of the combination in dioptre.
items.s: Powers of lenses in contact add directly, so the combination has power 2 + 2 = 4 dioptre.

items.q: A magnifying glass of focal length 5 cm is used with the eye relaxed. Taking the least distance of distinct vision as 25 cm, calculate its angular magnification.
items.s: The magnification is one plus the least distance of distinct vision divided by the focal length = 1 + 25/5 = 6.

items.q: A ray passes through a prism of angle 60 degrees with angles of refraction 25 degrees and 35 degrees at the two faces. Calculate the angle of deviation in degrees.
items.s: The deviation is the sum of the two angles of refraction less the prism angle = 25 + 35 - 60 = 0 degrees.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines real image?
o: a picture formed where rays actually meet, so that it can be caught on a screen
how far below the surface a submerged object seems to lie when viewed from directly above
the bouncing back of a parallel beam from a smooth surface so that the beam stays parallel
the ability of an instrument to show two close objects as separate
items.s: real image: a picture formed where rays actually meet, so that it can be caught on a screen. The other options describe resolving power, regular reflection, apparent depth.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Which statement correctly defines angle of deviation?
o: a number measuring how much light a fibre can gather, fixed by the indices of its layers
the point at which a beam parallel to the axis is brought together or from which it appears to spread
a device that allows only vibrations in one plane to pass through it
the turn between the direction of the incident ray and that of the emerging ray
items.s: angle of deviation: the turn between the direction of the incident ray and that of the emerging ray. The other options describe numerical aperture, principal focus, polariser.

items.q: astigmatism may be defined as
o: a defect in which near objects appear blurred because the image would form behind the retina
the change in the shape of the lens of the eye to focus on objects at different distances
a defect in which the eye focuses lines in different directions at different distances
a very thin flexible strand of glass that guides light along its length by repeated internal reflection
items.s: astigmatism: a defect in which the eye focuses lines in different directions at different distances. The other options describe long sight, optical fibre, accommodation.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: Which of the following best describes diverging lens?
o: the turn between the direction of the incident ray and that of the emerging ray
a piece of glass thinner at the middle that spreads a parallel beam outward
the visible light flux spreading through one unit of solid angle from a source of one candela
the distance between the centres of two neighbouring lines of a ruled surface
items.s: diverging lens: a piece of glass thinner at the middle that spreads a parallel beam outward. The other options describe grating constant, angle of deviation, lumen.

items.q: Which term is described by “a discrete packet of electromagnetic energy travelling at the speed of light”?
o: lux
luminous intensity
illuminance
photon
items.s: photon is a discrete packet of electromagnetic energy travelling at the speed of light.

items.q: Which of the following best describes law of reflection?
o: the condition in which more atoms occupy a higher energy state than a lower one
the rule that the sine of the incidence direction bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the bending direction
the rule that the angle between the incident ray and the normal equals the angle between the reflected ray and the normal
the visible light flux spreading through one unit of solid angle from a source of one candela
items.s: law of reflection: the rule that the angle between the incident ray and the normal equals the angle between the reflected ray and the normal. The other options describe population inversion, Snell law of refraction, lumen.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Which of the following best describes double refraction?
o: a second polarising device used to examine the state of polarisation of a beam
the splitting of a ray into two rays of different speeds inside certain crystals
a picture formed where rays actually meet, so that it can be caught on a screen
a very thin flexible strand of glass that guides light along its length by repeated internal reflection
items.s: double refraction: the splitting of a ray into two rays of different speeds inside certain crystals. The other options describe analyser, optical fibre, real image.

items.q: lumen may be defined as
o: the colour effects produced when light reflected from the two surfaces of a very shallow layer combines
the greatest inclination at which light may enter a fibre and still be guided
the visible light flux spreading through one unit of solid angle from a source of one candela
the width of the opening through which light enters an optical system
items.s: lumen: the visible light flux spreading through one unit of solid angle from a source of one candela. The other options describe aperture, thin film interference, acceptance angle.

items.q: Which of the following best describes virtual image?
o: a picture from which rays only appear to diverge, so that it cannot be caught on a screen
an instrument using two lens systems so that the picture from the first is enlarged again by the second
a very thin flexible strand of glass that guides light along its length by repeated internal reflection
the power of a lens whose focal length is one metre
items.s: virtual image: a picture from which rays only appear to diverge, so that it cannot be caught on a screen. The other options describe dioptre, compound microscope, optical fibre.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Which term is described by “the greatest inclination at which light may enter a fibre and still be guided”?
o: optical fibre
acceptance angle
laser
population inversion
items.s: acceptance angle is the greatest inclination at which light may enter a fibre and still be guided.

items.q: All of the following belong to Reflection at plane and curved mirrors EXCEPT
o: regular reflection
stimulated emission
diffuse reflection
law of reflection
items.s: Every other option belongs to Reflection at plane and curved mirrors. “stimulated emission” belongs to Optical fibres and modern optics, not Reflection at plane and curved mirrors.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: The statement “one of the alternate bright and dark bands produced on a screen by interfering light” describes which of the following?
o: destructive interference
fringe
path difference
constructive interference
items.s: fringe is one of the alternate bright and dark bands produced on a screen by interfering light.

items.q: The statement “a surface ruled with many closely spaced parallel lines used to spread light into spectra” describes which of the following?
o: grating
central maximum
resolving power
grating constant
items.s: grating is a surface ruled with many closely spaced parallel lines used to spread light into spectra.

items.q: Which of the following best describes far point?
o: a block of transparent material with two sloping faces that bends and separates a beam passing through it
the ratio of the size of the picture to the size of the object
the greatest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly without strain
the splitting of a ray into two rays of different speeds inside certain crystals
items.s: far point: the greatest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly without strain. The other options describe magnification, prism, double refraction.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: Which term is described by “a single converging lens held close to an object to make it appear larger”?
o: diverging lens
principal focus
magnifying glass
dioptre
items.s: magnifying glass is a single converging lens held close to an object to make it appear larger.

items.q: The statement “a piece of glass thicker at the middle that brings a parallel beam to a point” describes which of the following?
o: converging lens
lens formula
power of a lens
diverging lens
items.s: converging lens is a piece of glass thicker at the middle that brings a parallel beam to a point.

items.q: Which of the following best describes focal length of a mirror?
o: the distance from the pole to the point where a parallel beam is brought together
a surface ruled with many closely spaced parallel lines used to spread light into spectra
the power of a lens whose focal length is one metre
the distance between the centres of two neighbouring bright bands
items.s: focal length of a mirror: the distance from the pole to the point where a parallel beam is brought together. The other options describe fringe separation, grating, dioptre.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Which statement correctly defines focal length of a mirror?
o: the width of the opening through which light enters an optical system
the distance from the pole to the point where a parallel beam is brought together
the ability of a material to separate colours, measured by the difference of index across the spectrum
a defect in which distant objects appear blurred because the image forms in front of the retina
items.s: focal length of a mirror: the distance from the pole to the point where a parallel beam is brought together. The other options describe dispersive power, aperture, short sight.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: apparent depth may be defined as
o: a single converging lens held close to an object to make it appear larger
the rule that the light passing an analyser varies as the square of the cosine between the two directions
the reciprocal of the focal length expressed in metres, measured in dioptre
how far below the surface a submerged object seems to lie when viewed from directly above
items.s: apparent depth: how far below the surface a submerged object seems to lie when viewed from directly above. The other options describe Malus law of intensity, magnifying glass, power of a lens.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines secondary maximum?
o: the ability of a material to separate colours, measured by the difference of index across the spectrum
a picture formed where rays actually meet, so that it can be caught on a screen
a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern
the ability of an instrument to show two close objects as separate
items.s: secondary maximum: a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern. The other options describe real image, dispersive power, resolving power.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines photon?
o: a discrete packet of electromagnetic energy travelling at the speed of light
how far below the surface a submerged object seems to lie when viewed from directly above
a piece of glass thinner at the middle that spreads a parallel beam outward
the spreading of light round the edges of an obstacle or through a narrow opening
items.s: photon: a discrete packet of electromagnetic energy travelling at the speed of light. The other options describe diverging lens, diffraction, apparent depth.

items.q: interference may be defined as
o: the rule that the sine of the incidence direction bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the bending direction
the addition of two waves at a point to give a larger or smaller resultant
the total visible light energy leaving a source per second in all directions
the colour effects produced when light reflected from the two surfaces of a very shallow layer combines
items.s: interference: the addition of two waves at a point to give a larger or smaller resultant. The other options describe Snell law of refraction, luminous flux, thin film interference.

items.q: coherent sources may be defined as
o: two emitters that keep a constant phase relation so their waves can interfere steadily
a defect in which the eye focuses lines in different directions at different distances
the ability of a material to separate colours, measured by the difference of index across the spectrum
a picture formed where rays actually meet, so that it can be caught on a screen
items.s: coherent sources: two emitters that keep a constant phase relation so their waves can interfere steadily. The other options describe real image, dispersive power, astigmatism.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines destructive interference?
o: the ability of an instrument to show two close objects as separate
a block of transparent material with two sloping faces that bends and separates a beam passing through it
the addition of two waves out of step so that their effects cancel
the ability of a material to separate colours, measured by the difference of index across the spectrum
items.s: destructive interference: the addition of two waves out of step so that their effects cancel. The other options describe resolving power, prism, dispersive power.

items.q: The statement “the distance between the centres of two neighbouring bright bands” describes which of the following?
o: constructive interference
interference
fringe separation
destructive interference
items.s: fringe separation is the distance between the centres of two neighbouring bright bands.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines population inversion.
o: the condition in which more atoms occupy a higher energy state than a lower one
a source producing a narrow beam of coherent light of a single wavelength
the complete return of light into the denser medium when the angle of incidence exceeds a certain value
the spreading of light round the edges of an obstacle or through a narrow opening
items.s: population inversion: the condition in which more atoms occupy a higher energy state than a lower one. The other options describe diffraction, laser, total internal reflection.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ability of an instrument to show two close objects as separate”?
o: diffraction
resolving power
central maximum
aperture
items.s: resolving power is the ability of an instrument to show two close objects as separate.

items.q: angle of deviation may be defined as
o: the closest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly
the whole family of radiations travelling at the speed of light, arranged by wavelength
the ability of a material to separate colours, measured by the difference of index across the spectrum
the turn between the direction of the incident ray and that of the emerging ray
items.s: angle of deviation: the turn between the direction of the incident ray and that of the emerging ray. The other options describe dispersive power, near point, electromagnetic spectrum.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines fringe.
o: a number measuring how much light a fibre can gather, fixed by the indices of its layers
the distance between the centres of two neighbouring bright bands
the scattering of light in many directions from a rough surface
one of the alternate bright and dark bands produced on a screen by interfering light
items.s: fringe: one of the alternate bright and dark bands produced on a screen by interfering light. The other options describe numerical aperture, fringe separation, diffuse reflection.

items.q: The statement “the amount of visible light falling per unit area on a surface” describes which of the following?
o: illuminance
photon
inverse square law of illumination
luminous intensity
items.s: illuminance is the amount of visible light falling per unit area on a surface.

items.q: Which term is described by “the splitting of white light into its component colours by refraction”?
o: deviation without dispersion
prism
minimum deviation
dispersion
items.s: dispersion is the splitting of white light into its component colours by refraction.

items.q: core of a fibre may be defined as
o: the inner strand of higher refractive index through which light is guided
the ability of an instrument to show two close objects as separate
the spreading of light round the edges of an obstacle or through a narrow opening
the colour effects produced when light reflected from the two surfaces of a very shallow layer combines
items.s: core of a fibre: the inner strand of higher refractive index through which light is guided. The other options describe diffraction, thin film interference, resolving power.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines prism.
o: a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern
a piece of glass thicker at the middle that brings a parallel beam to a point
a block of transparent material with two sloping faces that bends and separates a beam passing through it
a picture from which rays only appear to diverge, so that it cannot be caught on a screen
items.s: prism: a block of transparent material with two sloping faces that bends and separates a beam passing through it. The other options describe converging lens, virtual image, secondary maximum.

items.q: Which of the following best describes interference?
o: the visible light flux spreading through one unit of solid angle from a source of one candela
a picture from which rays only appear to diverge, so that it cannot be caught on a screen
the ability of a material to separate colours, measured by the difference of index across the spectrum
the addition of two waves at a point to give a larger or smaller resultant
items.s: interference: the addition of two waves at a point to give a larger or smaller resultant. The other options describe dispersive power, virtual image, lumen.

items.q: Which of the following best describes coherent sources?
o: a defect in which near objects appear blurred because the image would form behind the retina
the band of colours produced when light is separated according to wavelength
the condition in which more atoms occupy a higher energy state than a lower one
two emitters that keep a constant phase relation so their waves can interfere steadily
items.s: coherent sources: two emitters that keep a constant phase relation so their waves can interfere steadily. The other options describe long sight, population inversion, spectrum.

items.q: Snell law of refraction may be defined as
o: the strength of a source as a producer of visible light, measured in candela
a defect in which near objects appear blurred because the image would form behind the retina
the band of colours produced when light is separated according to wavelength
the rule that the sine of the incidence direction bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the bending direction
items.s: Snell law of refraction: the rule that the sine of the incidence direction bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the bending direction. The other options describe long sight, luminous intensity, spectrum.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines short sight?
o: an instrument using two lens systems so that the picture from the first is enlarged again by the second
the closest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly
a defect in which distant objects appear blurred because the image forms in front of the retina
the change in the shape of the lens of the eye to focus on objects at different distances
items.s: short sight: a defect in which distant objects appear blurred because the image forms in front of the retina. The other options describe compound microscope, accommodation, near point.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: Which term is described by “a defect in which near objects appear blurred because the image would form behind the retina”?
o: astigmatism
long sight
near point
short sight
items.s: long sight is a defect in which near objects appear blurred because the image would form behind the retina.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: Which term is described by “the turning of the plane of polarisation by certain substances”?
o: optical activity
double refraction
polarisation
plane of vibration
items.s: optical activity is the turning of the plane of polarisation by certain substances.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Snell law of refraction.
o: a block of transparent material with two sloping faces that bends and separates a beam passing through it
the rule that the sine of the incidence direction bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the bending direction
the splitting of white light into its component colours by refraction
the condition in which more atoms occupy a higher energy state than a lower one
items.s: Snell law of refraction: the rule that the sine of the incidence direction bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the bending direction. The other options describe dispersion, population inversion, prism.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines polariser.
o: the addition of two waves out of step so that their effects cancel
the rule that the sine of the incidence direction bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the bending direction
a device that allows only vibrations in one plane to pass through it
the distance between the centres of two neighbouring lines of a ruled surface
items.s: polariser: a device that allows only vibrations in one plane to pass through it. The other options describe grating constant, Snell law of refraction, destructive interference.

items.q: stimulated emission may be defined as
o: the release of a second identical photon when one photon triggers an excited atom
the turning of the plane of polarisation by certain substances
the surface containing the direction of travel and the direction in which the disturbance moves
a surface ruled with many closely spaced parallel lines used to spread light into spectra
items.s: stimulated emission: the release of a second identical photon when one photon triggers an excited atom. The other options describe optical activity, plane of vibration, grating.

items.q: All of the following belong to Interference of light EXCEPT
o: path difference
laser
coherent sources
interference
items.s: Every other option belongs to Interference of light. “laser” belongs to Optical fibres and modern optics, not Interference of light.

items.q: secondary maximum may be defined as
o: the rule that the angle between the incident ray and the normal equals the angle between the reflected ray and the normal
a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern
a surface ruled with many closely spaced parallel lines used to spread light into spectra
the sideways shift of a ray after it passes through a parallel sided slab
items.s: secondary maximum: a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern. The other options describe grating, lateral displacement, law of reflection.

items.q: Which term is described by “the closest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly”?
o: accommodation
astigmatism
near point
far point
items.s: near point is the closest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: Which term is described by “the point at which a beam parallel to the axis is brought together or from which it appears to spread”?
o: compound microscope
magnifying glass
principal focus
dioptre
items.s: principal focus is the point at which a beam parallel to the axis is brought together or from which it appears to spread.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines resolving power?
o: the ability of an instrument to show two close objects as separate
the light sensitive layer at the back of the eye on which the picture is formed
the visible light flux spreading through one unit of solid angle from a source of one candela
the bouncing back of a parallel beam from a smooth surface so that the beam stays parallel
items.s: resolving power: the ability of an instrument to show two close objects as separate. The other options describe regular reflection, lumen, retina.

items.q: The statement “a picture formed where rays actually meet, so that it can be caught on a screen” describes which of the following?
o: real image
regular reflection
law of reflection
pole of a mirror
items.s: real image is a picture formed where rays actually meet, so that it can be caught on a screen.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Which of the following best describes constructive interference?
o: a second polarising device used to examine the state of polarisation of a beam
the addition of two waves in step so that their effects reinforce
the change in the shape of the lens of the eye to focus on objects at different distances
the addition of two waves at a point to give a larger or smaller resultant
items.s: constructive interference: the addition of two waves in step so that their effects reinforce. The other options describe accommodation, analyser, interference.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines virtual image.
o: a number measuring how much light a fibre can gather, fixed by the indices of its layers
the splitting of a ray into two rays of different speeds inside certain crystals
a picture from which rays only appear to diverge, so that it cannot be caught on a screen
the splitting of white light into its component colours by refraction
items.s: virtual image: a picture from which rays only appear to diverge, so that it cannot be caught on a screen. The other options describe dispersion, double refraction, numerical aperture.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Which term is described by “the distance between the centres of two neighbouring lines of a ruled surface”?
o: aperture
grating constant
central maximum
grating
items.s: grating constant is the distance between the centres of two neighbouring lines of a ruled surface.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines stimulated emission.
o: the release of a second identical photon when one photon triggers an excited atom
the loss of the ability to focus on near objects that comes with age
the turn between the direction of the incident ray and that of the emerging ray
a block of transparent material with two sloping faces that bends and separates a beam passing through it
items.s: stimulated emission: the release of a second identical photon when one photon triggers an excited atom. The other options describe angle of deviation, presbyopia, prism.

items.q: Which term is described by “the scattering of light in many directions from a rough surface”?
o: law of reflection
diffuse reflection
real image
magnification
items.s: diffuse reflection is the scattering of light in many directions from a rough surface.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines diffraction.
o: the ability of a material to separate colours, measured by the difference of index across the spectrum
the spreading of light round the edges of an obstacle or through a narrow opening
the point at which a beam parallel to the axis is brought together or from which it appears to spread
a piece of glass thinner at the middle that spreads a parallel beam outward
items.s: diffraction: the spreading of light round the edges of an obstacle or through a narrow opening. The other options describe principal focus, dispersive power, diverging lens.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines lateral displacement.
o: the restriction of the vibrations of a transverse wave to one plane
a piece of glass thinner at the middle that spreads a parallel beam outward
a surface ruled with many closely spaced parallel lines used to spread light into spectra
the sideways shift of a ray after it passes through a parallel sided slab
items.s: lateral displacement: the sideways shift of a ray after it passes through a parallel sided slab. The other options describe polarisation, grating, diverging lens.

items.q: retina may be defined as
o: the restriction of the vibrations of a transverse wave to one plane
the scattering of light in many directions from a rough surface
the splitting of a ray into two rays of different speeds inside certain crystals
the light sensitive layer at the back of the eye on which the picture is formed
items.s: retina: the light sensitive layer at the back of the eye on which the picture is formed. The other options describe double refraction, polarisation, diffuse reflection.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: Which statement correctly defines stimulated emission?
o: an instrument using two lens systems so that the picture from the first is enlarged again by the second
the central point of the reflecting surface where the principal axis meets it
the release of a second identical photon when one photon triggers an excited atom
the restriction of the vibrations of a transverse wave to one plane
items.s: stimulated emission: the release of a second identical photon when one photon triggers an excited atom. The other options describe pole of a mirror, compound microscope, polarisation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines angle of deviation.
o: the ratio of the size of the picture to the size of the object
the turn between the direction of the incident ray and that of the emerging ray
a defect in which distant objects appear blurred because the image forms in front of the retina
two emitters that keep a constant phase relation so their waves can interfere steadily
items.s: angle of deviation: the turn between the direction of the incident ray and that of the emerging ray. The other options describe magnification, short sight, coherent sources.

items.q: thin film interference may be defined as
o: a piece of glass thinner at the middle that spreads a parallel beam outward
the smallest bending produced by a prism, occurring when the ray passes symmetrically
the colour effects produced when light reflected from the two surfaces of a very shallow layer combines
the scattering of light in many directions from a rough surface
items.s: thin film interference: the colour effects produced when light reflected from the two surfaces of a very shallow layer combines. The other options describe diverging lens, minimum deviation, diffuse reflection.

items.q: illuminance may be defined as
o: a piece of glass thicker at the middle that brings a parallel beam to a point
the amount of visible light falling per unit area on a surface
the spreading of light round the edges of an obstacle or through a narrow opening
a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern
items.s: illuminance: the amount of visible light falling per unit area on a surface. The other options describe converging lens, diffraction, secondary maximum.

items.q: Which term is described by “how far below the surface a submerged object seems to lie when viewed from directly above”?
o: critical angle
apparent depth
lateral displacement
refraction
items.s: apparent depth is how far below the surface a submerged object seems to lie when viewed from directly above.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines polariser?
o: an instrument using two lens systems so that the picture from the first is enlarged again by the second
a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern
the visible light flux spreading through one unit of solid angle from a source of one candela
a device that allows only vibrations in one plane to pass through it
items.s: polariser: a device that allows only vibrations in one plane to pass through it. The other options describe compound microscope, lumen, secondary maximum.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines pole of a mirror.
o: the greatest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly without strain
the central point of the reflecting surface where the principal axis meets it
the bouncing back of a parallel beam from a smooth surface so that the beam stays parallel
the incidence direction at which the reflected beam is completely polarised
items.s: pole of a mirror: the central point of the reflecting surface where the principal axis meets it. The other options describe far point, Brewster angle, regular reflection.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines secondary maximum.
o: a second polarising device used to examine the state of polarisation of a beam
a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern
two emitters that keep a constant phase relation so their waves can interfere steadily
the outer layer of lower refractive index that keeps light inside the inner strand
items.s: secondary maximum: a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern. The other options describe coherent sources, cladding, analyser.

items.q: Which term is described by “one of the alternate bright and dark bands produced on a screen by interfering light”?
o: fringe
thin film interference
interference
path difference
items.s: fringe is one of the alternate bright and dark bands produced on a screen by interfering light.

items.q: An object stands 60 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 24 cm. Calculate the distance of the image from the mirror in cm.
items.s: Using the mirror relation, 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/24 - 1/60, so v = 40 cm.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: An object is placed 40 cm from a converging lens of focal length 25 cm. Calculate the image distance in cm.
items.s: From the lens relation 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/25 - 1/40, the image distance is 66.67 cm.

items.q: A magnifying glass of focal length 10 cm is used with the eye relaxed. Taking the least distance of distinct vision as 25 cm, calculate its angular magnification.
items.s: The magnification is one plus the least distance of distinct vision divided by the focal length = 1 + 25/10 = 3.5.

items.q: A ray passes through a prism of angle 60 degrees with angles of refraction 20 degrees and 40 degrees at the two faces. Calculate the angle of deviation in degrees.
items.s: The deviation is the sum of the two angles of refraction less the prism angle = 20 + 40 - 60 = 0 degrees.

items.q: In a two slit experiment the slits are 0.2 mm apart and the screen is 2.5 m away. Taking the wavelength as 450 nm, calculate the fringe separation in mm.
items.s: Fringe separation = wavelength x screen distance / slit separation = 450 x 10^-9 x 2.5 / (0.2 x 10^-3) = 5.62 mm.

items.q: Plane polarised light of intensity 500 units falls on an analyser set at 45 degrees to the plane of vibration. Calculate the intensity transmitted, in the same units.
items.s: By the cosine squared rule the transmitted intensity is 500 x cos squared 45 degrees = 250 units.

items.q: Light is guided along the core of refractive index 1.52 of an optical fibre surrounded by cladding of refractive index 1.46. Calculate the critical angle at the boundary, in degrees.
items.s: The critical angle satisfies sin(c) = 1.46/1.52 = 0.9605, so it equals 73.85 degrees.

items.q: A short sighted person can see clearly only up to 1 m. Calculate the power of the correcting lens needed, in dioptre.
items.s: The lens must form an image at the far point, so its focal length is minus 1 m and its power is -1/1 = -1 dioptre.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: A point source of luminous intensity 100 candela shines on a surface placed 1.5 m directly below it. Calculate the illuminance on the surface in lux.
items.s: Illuminance = intensity / distance squared = 100 / (1.5 x 1.5) = 44.44 lux.

items.q: Light of wavelength 500 nm falls on a surface. Taking the product of the Planck constant and the speed of light as 1.99 x 10^-25 J m, calculate the energy of one photon in units of 10^-19 J.
items.s: Photon energy = product of the Planck constant and the speed of light divided by wavelength = 1.99 x 10^-25 / (500 x 10^-9) = 3.18 units of 10^-19 J.

items.q: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 10 cm. Calculate its focal length in cm.
items.s: For a spherical mirror the focal length is half the radius of curvature = 10 / 2 = 5 cm.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: A plane mirror is turned through 30 degrees. Calculate the angle through which the reflected ray turns, in degrees.
items.s: Turning the mirror by an angle turns the reflected ray by twice that angle, so the answer is 60 degrees.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Light travels at 2.5 x 10^8 m/s in a certain medium. Taking the speed of light in a vacuum as 3.0 x 10^8 m/s, calculate the refractive index of the medium.
items.s: Refractive index = speed in a vacuum / speed in the medium = 3.0 / 2.5 = 1.2.

items.q: A ray strikes the surface of a medium of refractive index 1.33 at an angle of incidence of 45 degrees. Calculate the angle of refraction in degrees.
items.s: By the refraction relation sin r = sin 45 / 1.33 = 0.5317, so the angle of refraction is 32.12 degrees.

items.q: A ray passes normally through a glass slab of thickness 5 cm and refractive index 1.5. Calculate the lateral displacement of the ray in cm.
items.s: The sideways shift is thickness times (1 - 1/refractive index) = 5 x (1 - 1/1.5) = 1.67 cm.

items.q: An object 24 cm from a converging lens of focal length 15 cm forms an image. Calculate the magnification.
items.s: The image distance is 40 cm, so the magnification is v/u = 1.67.

items.q: Two thin lenses of power 10 dioptre and 4 dioptre are placed in contact. Calculate the power of the combination in dioptre.
items.s: Powers of lenses in contact add directly, so the combination has power 10 + 4 = 14 dioptre.

items.q: A compound microscope has an objective of magnification 5 and an eyepiece of magnification 10. Calculate the total magnification.
items.s: The magnifications of the two lens systems multiply, so the total is 5 x 10 = 50.

items.q: A prism of angle 30 degrees produces a minimum deviation of 38 degrees. Calculate the refractive index of its material.
items.s: At minimum deviation the index is sin((A + D)/2) / sin(A/2) = sin 34 / sin 15 = 2.16.

items.q: Two coherent waves of wavelength 500 nm meet at a point with a path difference of 1 wavelengths. Calculate the path difference in nm.
items.s: A path difference of 1 wavelengths is 1 x 500 = 500 nm, and since it is a whole number of wavelengths the point is bright.

items.q: Light falls normally on a soap film of refractive index 1.5 and thickness 600 nm. Calculate the optical path difference for light reflected from its two surfaces, in nm.
items.s: The extra distance is twice the thickness multiplied by the index = 2 x 1.5 x 600 = 1800 nm.

items.q: Two coherent beams of amplitudes in the ratio 4 to 5 interfere. Calculate the ratio of the maximum intensity to the minimum intensity.
items.s: The intensity ratio is the square of the sum of the amplitudes over the square of their difference = (4 + 5)^2 / (4 - 5)^2 = 81.

items.q: Light of wavelength 650 nm passes through a single slit of width 0.2 mm. Calculate the angle at which the first minimum appears, in degrees.
items.s: The first minimum satisfies sin(theta) = wavelength / slit width = 650 x 10^-9 / 0.2 x 10^-3, giving 0.1862 degrees.

items.q: A telescope objective has an aperture of 5 cm. Taking the wavelength as 650 nm, calculate the smallest angular separation it can resolve, in units of 10^-6 radian.
items.s: The limit is 1.22 times the wavelength divided by the aperture = 1.22 x 650 x 10^-9 / 0.05 = 0.1586 units of 10^-6 radian.

items.q: Light reflected from the surface of a medium of refractive index 1.45 is completely plane polarised. Calculate the angle of incidence in degrees.
items.s: The polarising angle satisfies tan(p) = 1.45, so the angle of incidence is 55.41 degrees.

items.q: A solution has a specific rotation of 60 degrees per dm per unit concentration and is placed in a tube of length 0.5 dm at a concentration of 10 g per cm cubed. Calculate the angle through which the plane of polarisation is turned, in degrees.
items.s: The angle turned is specific rotation x concentration x length = 60 x 0.5 x 10 = 300 degrees.

items.q: An optical fibre has a core of refractive index 1.52 and a cladding of refractive index 1.4. Calculate the acceptance angle in air, in degrees.
items.s: The sine of the acceptance angle is the square root of the difference of the squares of the indices = sqrt(2.31 - 1.96), giving 36.3 degrees.

items.q: An optical fibre has a core of refractive index 1.55 and a cladding of refractive index 1.4. Calculate its numerical aperture.
items.s: The numerical aperture is the square root of the difference of the squares of the two indices = sqrt(2.4 - 1.96) = 0.6652.

items.q: A laser of output power 20 mW is switched on for 2 s. Calculate the total energy it delivers in mJ.
items.s: Energy delivered = power x time = 20 x 10^-3 x 2 = 40 mJ.

items.q: A long sighted person has a near point of 0.6 m and wishes to read at 0.25 m. Calculate the power of the lens needed, in dioptre.
items.s: The lens must take an object at 0.25 m to an image at 0.6 m, so its power is 1/0.25 - 1/0.6 = 2.33 dioptre.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: An eye can focus clearly from a near point of 0.3 m out to a far point of 5 m. Calculate the range of power of its lens, in dioptre.
items.s: The change of power is 1/0.3 - 1/5 = 3.13 dioptre.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: A surface is lit to 100 lux by a lamp. Calculate the illuminance in lux when the surface is moved to 5 times its original distance from the lamp.
items.s: The illuminance varies inversely as the square of the distance, so it becomes 100 / (5 x 5) = 4 lux.

items.q: An object stands 60 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Calculate the distance of the image from the mirror in cm.
items.s: Using the mirror relation, 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/15 - 1/60, so v = 20 cm.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Light travels from a medium of refractive index 1.5 towards air. Calculate the critical angle in degrees.
items.s: The critical angle satisfies sin c = 1/1.5, so c = 41.81 degrees.

items.q: A coin lies at the bottom of a pool of water of depth 2 m. Taking the refractive index of water as 1.6, calculate the apparent depth of the coin in m.
items.s: Apparent depth = real depth / refractive index = 2 / 1.6 = 1.25 m.

items.q: An object is placed 40 cm from a converging lens of focal length 20 cm. Calculate the image distance in cm.
items.s: From the lens relation 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/20 - 1/40, the image distance is 40 cm.

items.q: A magnifying glass of focal length 8 cm is used with the eye relaxed. Taking the least distance of distinct vision as 25 cm, calculate its angular magnification.
items.s: The magnification is one plus the least distance of distinct vision divided by the focal length = 1 + 25/8 = 4.12.

items.q: In a two slit experiment the slits are 0.4 mm apart and the screen is 1.5 m away. Taking the wavelength as 550 nm, calculate the fringe separation in mm.
items.s: Fringe separation = wavelength x screen distance / slit separation = 550 x 10^-9 x 1.5 / (0.4 x 10^-3) = 2.06 mm.

items.q: Plane polarised light of intensity 800 units falls on an analyser set at 60 degrees to the plane of vibration. Calculate the intensity transmitted, in the same units.
items.s: By the cosine squared rule the transmitted intensity is 800 x cos squared 60 degrees = 200 units.

items.q: A short sighted person can see clearly only up to 1.5 m. Calculate the power of the correcting lens needed, in dioptre.
items.s: The lens must form an image at the far point, so its focal length is minus 1.5 m and its power is -1/1.5 = -0.6667 dioptre.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: A point source of luminous intensity 400 candela shines on a surface placed 2.5 m directly below it. Calculate the illuminance on the surface in lux.
items.s: Illuminance = intensity / distance squared = 400 / (2.5 x 2.5) = 64 lux.

items.q: Light of wavelength 650 nm falls on a surface. Taking the product of the Planck constant and the speed of light as 1.99 x 10^-25 J m, calculate the energy of one photon in units of 10^-19 J.
items.s: Photon energy = product of the Planck constant and the speed of light divided by wavelength = 1.99 x 10^-25 / (650 x 10^-9) = 2.44 units of 10^-19 J.

items.q: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 80 cm. Calculate its focal length in cm.
items.s: For a spherical mirror the focal length is half the radius of curvature = 80 / 2 = 40 cm.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: An object is placed 30 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 25 cm. Calculate the linear magnification produced.
items.s: The image distance works out to 150 cm, so the magnification is v/u = 5.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: A plane mirror is turned through 25 degrees. Calculate the angle through which the reflected ray turns, in degrees.
items.s: Turning the mirror by an angle turns the reflected ray by twice that angle, so the answer is 50 degrees.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: A ray strikes the surface of a medium of refractive index 1.6 at an angle of incidence of 45 degrees. Calculate the angle of refraction in degrees.
items.s: By the refraction relation sin r = sin 45 / 1.6 = 0.4419, so the angle of refraction is 26.23 degrees.

items.q: A ray passes normally through a glass slab of thickness 4 cm and refractive index 1.5. Calculate the lateral displacement of the ray in cm.
items.s: The sideways shift is thickness times (1 - 1/refractive index) = 4 x (1 - 1/1.5) = 1.33 cm.

items.q: A lens has a focal length of 40 cm. Calculate its power in dioptre.
items.s: Power in dioptre is one hundred divided by the focal length in centimetres = 100 / 40 = 2.5.

items.q: Two thin lenses of power 8 dioptre and -4 dioptre are placed in contact. Calculate the power of the combination in dioptre.
items.s: Powers of lenses in contact add directly, so the combination has power 8 + -4 = 4 dioptre.

items.q: A prism of angle 45 degrees produces a minimum deviation of 30 degrees. Calculate the refractive index of its material.
items.s: At minimum deviation the index is sin((A + D)/2) / sin(A/2) = sin 37.5 / sin 22.5 = 1.59.

items.q: A glass has refractive indices 1.52 for violet and 1.5 for red light. Taking the index for the middle of the spectrum as 1.51, calculate its dispersive power.
items.s: Dispersive power = (index for violet - index for red) / (middle index - 1) = (1.52 - 1.5)/(1.51 - 1) = 0.0392.

items.q: Two coherent waves of wavelength 500 nm meet at a point with a path difference of 2 wavelengths. Calculate the path difference in nm.
items.s: A path difference of 2 wavelengths is 2 x 500 = 1000 nm, and since it is a whole number of wavelengths the point is bright.

items.q: Light falls normally on a soap film of refractive index 1.4 and thickness 400 nm. Calculate the optical path difference for light reflected from its two surfaces, in nm.
items.s: The extra distance is twice the thickness multiplied by the index = 2 x 1.4 x 400 = 1120 nm.

items.q: Two coherent beams of amplitudes in the ratio 3 to 4 interfere. Calculate the ratio of the maximum intensity to the minimum intensity.
items.s: The intensity ratio is the square of the sum of the amplitudes over the square of their difference = (3 + 4)^2 / (3 - 4)^2 = 49.

items.q: A diffraction grating is ruled with 400 lines per millimetre. Calculate the distance between neighbouring lines in nm.
items.s: One millimetre contains 400 lines, so the spacing is 10^6 nm divided by 400 = 2500 nm.

items.q: Light of wavelength 500 nm passes through a single slit of width 0.25 mm. Calculate the angle at which the first minimum appears, in degrees.
items.s: The first minimum satisfies sin(theta) = wavelength / slit width = 500 x 10^-9 / 0.25 x 10^-3, giving 0.1146 degrees.

items.q: A telescope objective has an aperture of 4 cm. Taking the wavelength as 550 nm, calculate the smallest angular separation it can resolve, in units of 10^-6 radian.
items.s: The limit is 1.22 times the wavelength divided by the aperture = 1.22 x 550 x 10^-9 / 0.04 = 0.1678 units of 10^-6 radian.

items.q: Light reflected from the surface of a medium of refractive index 1.65 is completely plane polarised. Calculate the angle of incidence in degrees.
items.s: The polarising angle satisfies tan(p) = 1.65, so the angle of incidence is 58.78 degrees.

items.q: Unpolarised light of intensity 400 units passes through a single polarising sheet. Calculate the intensity of the transmitted beam in the same units.
items.s: A single sheet passes half the intensity of unpolarised light, so the transmitted value is 400 / 2 = 200 units.

items.q: A solution has a specific rotation of 60 degrees per dm per unit concentration and is placed in a tube of length 0.2 dm at a concentration of 20 g per cm cubed. Calculate the angle through which the plane of polarisation is turned, in degrees.
items.s: The angle turned is specific rotation x concentration x length = 60 x 0.2 x 20 = 240 degrees.

items.q: The best definition of central maximum among these is
o: a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern
the wide bright band formed straight ahead of the opening in a diffraction pattern
the ability of an instrument to show two close objects as separate
a surface ruled with many closely spaced parallel lines used to spread light into spectra
items.s: central maximum: the wide bright band formed straight ahead of the opening in a diffraction pattern. The other options describe grating, secondary maximum, resolving power.

items.q: The statement “the width of the opening through which light enters an optical system” describes which of the following?
o: secondary maximum
single slit pattern
diffraction
aperture
items.s: aperture is the width of the opening through which light enters an optical system.

items.q: The best definition of Malus law of intensity among these is
o: the turning of the plane of polarisation by certain substances
the surface containing the direction of travel and the direction in which the disturbance moves
the rule that the light passing an analyser varies as the square of the cosine between the two directions
the restriction of the vibrations of a transverse wave to one plane
items.s: Malus law of intensity: the rule that the light passing an analyser varies as the square of the cosine between the two directions. The other options describe plane of vibration, optical activity, polarisation.

items.q: cladding is best described as
o: the greatest inclination at which light may enter a fibre and still be guided

items.q: An object is placed 40 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. Calculate the linear magnification produced.
items.s: The image distance works out to 40 cm, so the magnification is v/u = 1.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: An object 20 cm from a converging lens of focal length 25 cm forms an image. Calculate the magnification.
items.s: The image distance is -100 cm, so the magnification is v/u = -5.

items.q: Two thin lenses of power 2.5 dioptre and 5 dioptre are placed in contact. Calculate the power of the combination in dioptre.
items.s: Powers of lenses in contact add directly, so the combination has power 2.5 + 5 = 7.5 dioptre.

items.q: Light of wavelength 400 nm passes through a single slit of width 0.25 mm. Calculate the angle at which the first minimum appears, in degrees.
items.s: The first minimum satisfies sin(theta) = wavelength / slit width = 400 x 10^-9 / 0.25 x 10^-3, giving 0.0917 degrees.

items.q: Light reflected from the surface of a medium of refractive index 1.5 is completely plane polarised. Calculate the angle of incidence in degrees.
items.s: The polarising angle satisfies tan(p) = 1.5, so the angle of incidence is 56.31 degrees.

items.q: An optical fibre has a core of refractive index 1.52 and a cladding of refractive index 1.45. Calculate the acceptance angle in air, in degrees.
items.s: The sine of the acceptance angle is the square root of the difference of the squares of the indices = sqrt(2.31 - 2.1), giving 27.13 degrees.

items.q: An optical fibre has a core of refractive index 1.6 and a cladding of refractive index 1.48. Calculate its numerical aperture.
items.s: The numerical aperture is the square root of the difference of the squares of the two indices = sqrt(2.56 - 2.19) = 0.6079.

items.q: A long sighted person has a near point of 1 m and wishes to read at 0.25 m. Calculate the power of the lens needed, in dioptre.
items.s: The lens must take an object at 0.25 m to an image at 1 m, so its power is 1/0.25 - 1/1 = 3 dioptre.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: A point source of luminous intensity 500 candela shines on a surface placed 4 m directly below it. Calculate the illuminance on the surface in lux.
items.s: Illuminance = intensity / distance squared = 500 / (4 x 4) = 31.25 lux.

items.q: A surface is lit to 40 lux by a lamp. Calculate the illuminance in lux when the surface is moved to 2 times its original distance from the lamp.
items.s: The illuminance varies inversely as the square of the distance, so it becomes 40 / (2 x 2) = 10 lux.

items.q: An object stands 30 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Calculate the distance of the image from the mirror in cm.
items.s: Using the mirror relation, 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/15 - 1/30, so v = 30 cm.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Light travels from a medium of refractive index 1.4 towards air. Calculate the critical angle in degrees.
items.s: The critical angle satisfies sin c = 1/1.4, so c = 45.58 degrees.

items.q: A coin lies at the bottom of a pool of water of depth 2 m. Taking the refractive index of water as 1.5, calculate the apparent depth of the coin in m.
items.s: Apparent depth = real depth / refractive index = 2 / 1.5 = 1.33 m.

items.q: A ray passes normally through a glass slab of thickness 6 cm and refractive index 1.4. Calculate the lateral displacement of the ray in cm.
items.s: The sideways shift is thickness times (1 - 1/refractive index) = 6 x (1 - 1/1.4) = 1.71 cm.

items.q: An object is placed 30 cm from a converging lens of focal length 25 cm. Calculate the image distance in cm.
items.s: From the lens relation 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/25 - 1/30, the image distance is 150 cm.

items.q: A compound microscope has an objective of magnification 4 and an eyepiece of magnification 10. Calculate the total magnification.
items.s: The magnifications of the two lens systems multiply, so the total is 4 x 10 = 40.

items.q: A ray passes through a prism of angle 50 degrees with angles of refraction 25 degrees and 25 degrees at the two faces. Calculate the angle of deviation in degrees.
items.s: The deviation is the sum of the two angles of refraction less the prism angle = 25 + 25 - 50 = 0 degrees.

items.q: A glass has refractive indices 1.53 for violet and 1.51 for red light. Taking the index for the middle of the spectrum as 1.52, calculate its dispersive power.
items.s: Dispersive power = (index for violet - index for red) / (middle index - 1) = (1.53 - 1.51)/(1.52 - 1) = 0.0385.

items.q: In a two slit experiment the slits are 0.4 mm apart and the screen is 2.5 m away. Taking the wavelength as 600 nm, calculate the fringe separation in mm.
items.s: Fringe separation = wavelength x screen distance / slit separation = 600 x 10^-9 x 2.5 / (0.4 x 10^-3) = 3.75 mm.

items.q: A diffraction grating is ruled with 200 lines per millimetre. Calculate the distance between neighbouring lines in nm.
items.s: One millimetre contains 200 lines, so the spacing is 10^6 nm divided by 200 = 5000 nm.

items.q: A telescope objective has an aperture of 25 cm. Taking the wavelength as 600 nm, calculate the smallest angular separation it can resolve, in units of 10^-6 radian.
items.s: The limit is 1.22 times the wavelength divided by the aperture = 1.22 x 600 x 10^-9 / 0.25 = 0.0293 units of 10^-6 radian.

items.q: Plane polarised light of intensity 500 units falls on an analyser set at 0 degrees to the plane of vibration. Calculate the intensity transmitted, in the same units.
items.s: By the cosine squared rule the transmitted intensity is 500 x cos squared 0 degrees = 500 units.

items.q: Unpolarised light of intensity 100 units passes through a single polarising sheet. Calculate the intensity of the transmitted beam in the same units.
items.s: A single sheet passes half the intensity of unpolarised light, so the transmitted value is 100 / 2 = 50 units.

items.q: A solution has a specific rotation of 25 degrees per dm per unit concentration and is placed in a tube of length 0.5 dm at a concentration of 20 g per cm cubed. Calculate the angle through which the plane of polarisation is turned, in degrees.
items.s: The angle turned is specific rotation x concentration x length = 25 x 0.5 x 20 = 250 degrees.

items.q: A laser of output power 2 mW is switched on for 5 s. Calculate the total energy it delivers in mJ.
items.s: Energy delivered = power x time = 2 x 10^-3 x 5 = 10 mJ.

items.q: A short sighted person can see clearly only up to 2 m. Calculate the power of the correcting lens needed, in dioptre.
items.s: The lens must form an image at the far point, so its focal length is minus 2 m and its power is -1/2 = -0.5 dioptre.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: An eye can focus clearly from a near point of 0.3 m out to a far point of 1 m. Calculate the range of power of its lens, in dioptre.
items.s: The change of power is 1/0.3 - 1/1 = 2.33 dioptre.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: Light of wavelength 550 nm falls on a surface. Taking the product of the Planck constant and the speed of light as 1.99 x 10^-25 J m, calculate the energy of one photon in units of 10^-19 J.
items.s: Photon energy = product of the Planck constant and the speed of light divided by wavelength = 1.99 x 10^-25 / (550 x 10^-9) = 2.89 units of 10^-19 J.

items.q: An object is placed 40 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 30 cm. Calculate the linear magnification produced.
items.s: The image distance works out to 120 cm, so the magnification is v/u = 3.

items.q: A ray strikes the surface of a medium of refractive index 1.5 at an angle of incidence of 25 degrees. Calculate the angle of refraction in degrees.
items.s: By the refraction relation sin r = sin 25 / 1.5 = 0.2817, so the angle of refraction is 16.36 degrees.

items.q: An object 50 cm from a converging lens of focal length 25 cm forms an image. Calculate the magnification.
items.s: The image distance is 50 cm, so the magnification is v/u = 1.

items.q: Two thin lenses of power 8 dioptre and 2.5 dioptre are placed in contact. Calculate the power of the combination in dioptre.
items.s: Powers of lenses in contact add directly, so the combination has power 8 + 2.5 = 10.5 dioptre.

items.q: Light falls normally on a soap film of refractive index 1.4 and thickness 600 nm. Calculate the optical path difference for light reflected from its two surfaces, in nm.
items.s: The extra distance is twice the thickness multiplied by the index = 2 x 1.4 x 600 = 1680 nm.

items.q: Light of wavelength 650 nm passes through a single slit of width 0.1 mm. Calculate the angle at which the first minimum appears, in degrees.
items.s: The first minimum satisfies sin(theta) = wavelength / slit width = 650 x 10^-9 / 0.1 x 10^-3, giving 0.3724 degrees.

items.q: Light reflected from the surface of a medium of refractive index 2.4 is completely plane polarised. Calculate the angle of incidence in degrees.
items.s: The polarising angle satisfies tan(p) = 2.4, so the angle of incidence is 67.38 degrees.

items.q: An optical fibre has a core of refractive index 1.55 and a cladding of refractive index 1.45. Calculate its numerical aperture.
items.s: The numerical aperture is the square root of the difference of the squares of the two indices = sqrt(2.4 - 2.1) = 0.5477.

items.q: A point source of luminous intensity 50 candela shines on a surface placed 2.5 m directly below it. Calculate the illuminance on the surface in lux.
items.s: Illuminance = intensity / distance squared = 50 / (2.5 x 2.5) = 8 lux.

items.q: A surface is lit to 20 lux by a lamp. Calculate the illuminance in lux when the surface is moved to 3 times its original distance from the lamp.
items.s: The illuminance varies inversely as the square of the distance, so it becomes 20 / (3 x 3) = 2.22 lux.

items.q: A plane mirror is turned through 15 degrees. Calculate the angle through which the reflected ray turns, in degrees.
items.s: Turning the mirror by an angle turns the reflected ray by twice that angle, so the answer is 30 degrees.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: A transparent medium has a refractive index of 1.65. Taking the speed of light in a vacuum as 3.0 x 10^8 m/s, calculate the speed of light in the medium in units of 10^8 m/s.
items.s: The speed in the medium is the speed in a vacuum divided by the index = 3.0 / 1.65 = 1.82 units of 10^8 m/s.

items.q: A coin lies at the bottom of a pool of water of depth 1 m. Taking the refractive index of water as 1.5, calculate the apparent depth of the coin in m.
items.s: Apparent depth = real depth / refractive index = 1 / 1.5 = 0.6667 m.

items.q: A ray passes normally through a glass slab of thickness 5 cm and refractive index 1.4. Calculate the lateral displacement of the ray in cm.
items.s: The sideways shift is thickness times (1 - 1/refractive index) = 5 x (1 - 1/1.4) = 1.43 cm.

items.q: An object is placed 60 cm from a converging lens of focal length 12 cm. Calculate the image distance in cm.
items.s: From the lens relation 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/12 - 1/60, the image distance is 15 cm.

items.q: A magnifying glass of focal length 12 cm is used with the eye relaxed. Taking the least distance of distinct vision as 25 cm, calculate its angular magnification.
items.s: The magnification is one plus the least distance of distinct vision divided by the focal length = 1 + 25/12 = 3.08.

items.q: A prism of angle 50 degrees produces a minimum deviation of 30 degrees. Calculate the refractive index of its material.
items.s: At minimum deviation the index is sin((A + D)/2) / sin(A/2) = sin 40 / sin 25 = 1.52.

items.q: A glass has refractive indices 1.54 for violet and 1.51 for red light. Taking the index for the middle of the spectrum as 1.52, calculate its dispersive power.
items.s: Dispersive power = (index for violet - index for red) / (middle index - 1) = (1.54 - 1.51)/(1.52 - 1) = 0.0577.

items.q: In a two slit experiment the slits are 0.25 mm apart and the screen is 1.5 m away. Taking the wavelength as 600 nm, calculate the fringe separation in mm.
items.s: Fringe separation = wavelength x screen distance / slit separation = 600 x 10^-9 x 1.5 / (0.25 x 10^-3) = 3.6 mm.

items.q: Two coherent beams of amplitudes in the ratio 1 to 3 interfere. Calculate the ratio of the maximum intensity to the minimum intensity.
items.s: The intensity ratio is the square of the sum of the amplitudes over the square of their difference = (1 + 3)^2 / (1 - 3)^2 = 4.

items.q: Light is guided along the core of refractive index 1.5 of an optical fibre surrounded by cladding of refractive index 1.45. Calculate the critical angle at the boundary, in degrees.
items.s: The critical angle satisfies sin(c) = 1.45/1.5 = 0.9667, so it equals 75.16 degrees.
