items.q: The correct meaning of principal focus is
o: a piece of glass thinner at the middle that spreads a parallel beam outward
an instrument using two lens systems so that the picture from the first is enlarged again by the second
the point at which a beam parallel to the axis is brought together or from which it appears to spread
a piece of glass thicker at the middle that brings a parallel beam to a point
items.s: principal focus: the point at which a beam parallel to the axis is brought together or from which it appears to spread. The other options describe converging lens, compound microscope, diverging lens.

items.q: The correct meaning of power of a lens is
o: the reciprocal of the focal length expressed in metres, measured in dioptre
a single converging lens held close to an object to make it appear larger
an instrument using two lens systems so that the picture from the first is enlarged again by the second
the power of a lens whose focal length is one metre
items.s: power of a lens: the reciprocal of the focal length expressed in metres, measured in dioptre. The other options describe compound microscope, dioptre, magnifying glass.

items.q: near point may be defined as
o: the loss of the ability to focus on near objects that comes with age
the closest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly
a defect in which distant objects appear blurred because the image forms in front of the retina
the greatest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly without strain
items.s: near point: the closest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly. The other options describe far point, short sight, presbyopia.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: The correct meaning of photon is
o: the rule that the light falling on a surface from a point emitter weakens as the second power of the separation
the whole family of radiations travelling at the speed of light, arranged by wavelength
a discrete packet of electromagnetic energy travelling at the speed of light
the amount of visible light falling per unit area on a surface
items.s: photon: a discrete packet of electromagnetic energy travelling at the speed of light. The other options describe inverse square law of illumination, illuminance, electromagnetic spectrum.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the closest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly”
o: accommodation
presbyopia
astigmatism
near point
items.s: near point is the closest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: The correct meaning of resolving power is
o: the width of the opening through which light enters an optical system
the spreading of light round the edges of an obstacle or through a narrow opening
the ability of an instrument to show two close objects as separate
the wide bright band formed straight ahead of the opening in a diffraction pattern
items.s: resolving power: the ability of an instrument to show two close objects as separate. The other options describe diffraction, central maximum, aperture.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines magnification?
o: the scattering of light in many directions from a rough surface
the ratio of the size of the picture to the size of the object
the bouncing back of a parallel beam from a smooth surface so that the beam stays parallel
the rule that the angle between the incident ray and the normal equals the angle between the reflected ray and the normal
items.s: magnification: the ratio of the size of the picture to the size of the object. The other options describe diffuse reflection, law of reflection, regular reflection.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains real image.
o: the ratio of the size of the picture to the size of the object
the bouncing back of a parallel beam from a smooth surface so that the beam stays parallel
a picture formed where rays actually meet, so that it can be caught on a screen
a picture from which rays only appear to diverge, so that it cannot be caught on a screen
items.s: real image: a picture formed where rays actually meet, so that it can be caught on a screen. The other options describe regular reflection, magnification, virtual image.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Which statement correctly defines refraction?
o: the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to its speed in a medium
the bending of light as it crosses the boundary between two transparent media
the property of a medium that makes light travel more slowly through it
the rule that the sine of the incidence direction bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the bending direction
items.s: refraction: the bending of light as it crosses the boundary between two transparent media. The other options describe Snell law of refraction, optical density, refractive index.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines accommodation?
o: a defect in which the eye focuses lines in different directions at different distances
a defect in which distant objects appear blurred because the image forms in front of the retina
a defect in which near objects appear blurred because the image would form behind the retina
the change in the shape of the lens of the eye to focus on objects at different distances
items.s: accommodation: the change in the shape of the lens of the eye to focus on objects at different distances. The other options describe long sight, short sight, astigmatism.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: “the condition in which more atoms occupy a higher energy state than a lower one” is the definition of
o: population inversion
stimulated emission
numerical aperture
optical fibre
items.s: population inversion is the condition in which more atoms occupy a higher energy state than a lower one.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains refraction.
o: the complete return of light into the denser medium when the angle of incidence exceeds a certain value
the bending of light as it crosses the boundary between two transparent media
how far below the surface a submerged object seems to lie when viewed from directly above
the rule that the sine of the incidence direction bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the bending direction
items.s: refraction: the bending of light as it crosses the boundary between two transparent media. The other options describe total internal reflection, apparent depth, Snell law of refraction.

items.q: “the strength of a source as a producer of visible light, measured in candela” is the definition of
o: lumen
luminous intensity
lux
luminous flux
items.s: luminous intensity is the strength of a source as a producer of visible light, measured in candela.

items.q: The correct meaning of dispersion is
o: the bending of a beam by a prism combination with no separation of its colours
two lenses of different materials cemented together so that colour separation cancels
the splitting of white light into its component colours by refraction
the ability of a material to separate colours, measured by the difference of index across the spectrum
items.s: dispersion: the splitting of white light into its component colours by refraction. The other options describe dispersive power, achromatic combination, deviation without dispersion.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines near point?
o: a defect in which distant objects appear blurred because the image forms in front of the retina
the closest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly
the light sensitive layer at the back of the eye on which the picture is formed
a defect in which near objects appear blurred because the image would form behind the retina
items.s: near point: the closest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly. The other options describe short sight, long sight, retina.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: “the loss of the ability to focus on near objects that comes with age” is the definition of
o: near point
astigmatism
accommodation
presbyopia
items.s: presbyopia is the loss of the ability to focus on near objects that comes with age.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: “the scattering of light in many directions from a rough surface” is the definition of
o: real image
focal length of a mirror
diffuse reflection
pole of a mirror
items.s: diffuse reflection is the scattering of light in many directions from a rough surface.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: “a block of transparent material with two sloping faces that bends and separates a beam passing through it” is the definition of
o: angle of deviation
deviation without dispersion
prism
achromatic combination
items.s: prism is a block of transparent material with two sloping faces that bends and separates a beam passing through it.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains double refraction.
o: the splitting of a ray into two rays of different speeds inside certain crystals
the restriction of the vibrations of a transverse wave to one plane
the rule that the light passing an analyser varies as the square of the cosine between the two directions
the incidence direction at which the reflected beam is completely polarised
items.s: double refraction: the splitting of a ray into two rays of different speeds inside certain crystals. The other options describe Brewster angle, Malus law of intensity, polarisation.

items.q: “an instrument using two lens systems so that the picture from the first is enlarged again by the second” is the definition of
o: magnifying glass
compound microscope
converging lens
dioptre
items.s: compound microscope is an instrument using two lens systems so that the picture from the first is enlarged again by the second.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines principal focus?
o: the point at which a beam parallel to the axis is brought together or from which it appears to spread
a piece of glass thicker at the middle that brings a parallel beam to a point
a single converging lens held close to an object to make it appear larger
a piece of glass thinner at the middle that spreads a parallel beam outward
items.s: principal focus: the point at which a beam parallel to the axis is brought together or from which it appears to spread. The other options describe magnifying glass, diverging lens, converging lens.

items.q: In this course, fringe separation refers to
o: the extra distance one wave travels compared with another to reach the same point
the addition of two waves at a point to give a larger or smaller resultant
the distance between the centres of two neighbouring bright bands
one of the alternate bright and dark bands produced on a screen by interfering light
items.s: fringe separation: the distance between the centres of two neighbouring bright bands. The other options describe interference, path difference, fringe.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Snell law of refraction?
o: the bending of light as it crosses the boundary between two transparent media
the complete return of light into the denser medium when the angle of incidence exceeds a certain value
the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to its speed in a medium
the rule that the sine of the incidence direction bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the bending direction
items.s: Snell law of refraction: the rule that the sine of the incidence direction bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the bending direction. The other options describe refraction, refractive index, total internal reflection.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a defect in which the eye focuses lines in different directions at different distances”
o: short sight
near point
astigmatism
accommodation
items.s: astigmatism is a defect in which the eye focuses lines in different directions at different distances.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: minimum deviation may be defined as
o: the splitting of white light into its component colours by refraction
a block of transparent material with two sloping faces that bends and separates a beam passing through it
the smallest bending produced by a prism, occurring when the ray passes symmetrically
the bending of a beam by a prism combination with no separation of its colours
items.s: minimum deviation: the smallest bending produced by a prism, occurring when the ray passes symmetrically. The other options describe dispersion, prism, deviation without dispersion.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the light sensitive layer at the back of the eye on which the picture is formed”
o: astigmatism
presbyopia
retina
far point
items.s: retina is the light sensitive layer at the back of the eye on which the picture is formed.
items.t: The eye and defects of vision

items.q: Which statement correctly defines diffuse reflection?
o: the scattering of light in many directions from a rough surface
the central point of the reflecting surface where the principal axis meets it
the ratio of the size of the picture to the size of the object
a picture from which rays only appear to diverge, so that it cannot be caught on a screen
items.s: diffuse reflection: the scattering of light in many directions from a rough surface. The other options describe magnification, virtual image, pole of a mirror.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains compound microscope.
o: the power of a lens whose focal length is one metre
a piece of glass thicker at the middle that brings a parallel beam to a point
a piece of glass thinner at the middle that spreads a parallel beam outward
an instrument using two lens systems so that the picture from the first is enlarged again by the second
items.s: compound microscope: an instrument using two lens systems so that the picture from the first is enlarged again by the second. The other options describe diverging lens, dioptre, converging lens.

items.q: “the surface containing the direction of travel and the direction in which the disturbance moves” is the definition of
o: polariser
polarisation
plane of vibration
analyser
items.s: plane of vibration is the surface containing the direction of travel and the direction in which the disturbance moves.

items.q: The correct meaning of apparent depth is
o: the property of a medium that makes light travel more slowly through it
the incidence direction in the denser medium for which the refracted ray grazes the boundary
how far below the surface a submerged object seems to lie when viewed from directly above
the rule that the sine of the incidence direction bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the bending direction
items.s: apparent depth: how far below the surface a submerged object seems to lie when viewed from directly above. The other options describe Snell law of refraction, optical density, critical angle.

items.q: In this course, magnification refers to
o: the bouncing back of a parallel beam from a smooth surface so that the beam stays parallel
the distance from the pole to the point where a parallel beam is brought together
the central point of the reflecting surface where the principal axis meets it
the ratio of the size of the picture to the size of the object
items.s: magnification: the ratio of the size of the picture to the size of the object. The other options describe regular reflection, pole of a mirror, focal length of a mirror.
items.t: Reflection at plane and curved mirrors

items.q: The correct meaning of central maximum is
o: a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern
a surface ruled with many closely spaced parallel lines used to spread light into spectra
the banded distribution of light produced when a beam passes through one narrow opening
the wide bright band formed straight ahead of the opening in a diffraction pattern
items.s: central maximum: the wide bright band formed straight ahead of the opening in a diffraction pattern. The other options describe grating, secondary maximum, single slit pattern.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines prism?
o: the ability of a material to separate colours, measured by the difference of index across the spectrum
the band of colours produced when light is separated according to wavelength
a block of transparent material with two sloping faces that bends and separates a beam passing through it
two lenses of different materials cemented together so that colour separation cancels
items.s: prism: a block of transparent material with two sloping faces that bends and separates a beam passing through it. The other options describe dispersive power, achromatic combination, spectrum.

items.q: “the band of colours produced when light is separated according to wavelength” is the definition of
o: angle of deviation
dispersion
spectrum
prism
items.s: spectrum is the band of colours produced when light is separated according to wavelength.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the spreading of light round the edges of an obstacle or through a narrow opening”
o: diffraction
resolving power
secondary maximum
grating constant
items.s: diffraction is the spreading of light round the edges of an obstacle or through a narrow opening.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains destructive interference.
o: the colour effects produced when light reflected from the two surfaces of a very shallow layer combines
the extra distance one wave travels compared with another to reach the same point
the addition of two waves out of step so that their effects cancel
two emitters that keep a constant phase relation so their waves can interfere steadily
items.s: destructive interference: the addition of two waves out of step so that their effects cancel. The other options describe thin film interference, path difference, coherent sources.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines analyser?
o: a second polarising device used to examine the state of polarisation of a beam
the splitting of a ray into two rays of different speeds inside certain crystals
the turning of the plane of polarisation by certain substances
the incidence direction at which the reflected beam is completely polarised
items.s: analyser: a second polarising device used to examine the state of polarisation of a beam. The other options describe double refraction, Brewster angle, optical activity.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains illuminance.
o: the illuminance produced when one lumen falls on one square metre of surface
the amount of visible light falling per unit area on a surface
the rule that the light falling on a surface from a point emitter weakens as the second power of the separation
the whole family of radiations travelling at the speed of light, arranged by wavelength
items.s: illuminance: the amount of visible light falling per unit area on a surface. The other options describe lux, electromagnetic spectrum, inverse square law of illumination.

items.q: “the bending of a beam by a prism combination with no separation of its colours” is the definition of
o: angle of deviation
deviation without dispersion
dispersion
prism
items.s: deviation without dispersion is the bending of a beam by a prism combination with no separation of its colours.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains achromatic combination.
o: the ability of a material to separate colours, measured by the difference of index across the spectrum
the bending of a beam by a prism combination with no separation of its colours
the splitting of white light into its component colours by refraction
two lenses of different materials cemented together so that colour separation cancels
items.s: achromatic combination: two lenses of different materials cemented together so that colour separation cancels. The other options describe dispersion, dispersive power, deviation without dispersion.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the amount of visible light falling per unit area on a surface”
o: electromagnetic spectrum
photon
lux
illuminance
items.s: illuminance is the amount of visible light falling per unit area on a surface.

two emitters that keep a constant phase relation so their waves can interfere steadily

items.q: “the addition of two waves at a point to give a larger or smaller resultant” is the definition of
o: interference
path difference
destructive interference
fringe separation
items.s: interference is the addition of two waves at a point to give a larger or smaller resultant.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the rule that the light falling on a surface from a point emitter weakens as the second power of the separation”
o: lux
inverse square law of illumination
photon
luminous intensity
items.s: inverse square law of illumination is the rule that the light falling on a surface from a point emitter weakens as the second power of the separation.

items.q: The correct meaning of stimulated emission is
o: the release of a second identical photon when one photon triggers an excited atom
the greatest inclination at which light may enter a fibre and still be guided
a source producing a narrow beam of coherent light of a single wavelength
a very thin flexible strand of glass that guides light along its length by repeated internal reflection
items.s: stimulated emission: the release of a second identical photon when one photon triggers an excited atom. The other options describe acceptance angle, optical fibre, laser.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines luminous flux?
o: the total visible light energy leaving a source per second in all directions
the illuminance produced when one lumen falls on one square metre of surface
the amount of visible light falling per unit area on a surface
the whole family of radiations travelling at the speed of light, arranged by wavelength
items.s: luminous flux: the total visible light energy leaving a source per second in all directions. The other options describe electromagnetic spectrum, illuminance, lux.

the whole family of radiations travelling at the speed of light, arranged by wavelength

o: a defect in which distant objects appear blurred because the image forms in front of the retina
a defect in which near objects appear blurred because the image would form behind the retina
the light sensitive layer at the back of the eye on which the picture is formed
the greatest distance at which the eye can focus an object clearly without strain
items.s: long sight: a defect in which near objects appear blurred because the image would form behind the retina. The other options describe far point, retina, short sight.

items.q: The correct meaning of secondary maximum is
o: the wide bright band formed straight ahead of the opening in a diffraction pattern
the banded distribution of light produced when a beam passes through one narrow opening
a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern
the distance between the centres of two neighbouring lines of a ruled surface
items.s: secondary maximum: a weaker bright band on either side of the central band of a diffraction pattern. The other options describe single slit pattern, grating constant, central maximum.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines dispersion?
o: a block of transparent material with two sloping faces that bends and separates a beam passing through it
the turn between the direction of the incident ray and that of the emerging ray
the splitting of white light into its component colours by refraction
the smallest bending produced by a prism, occurring when the ray passes symmetrically
items.s: dispersion: the splitting of white light into its component colours by refraction. The other options describe angle of deviation, minimum deviation, prism.
